subject: Simulation of objects in groups for DSsim

messages.author: ba2513683f4e548a
messages.subject: Simulation of objects in groups for DSsim
parts:
Hi everybody

I am preparing a project to assess feasibility of UAVs for surveying guanacos, a large ungulate that has social structure (forms family and juveniles groups).

The plan is to use strip transects as a way to survey the populations. Then we will compare p´citures at regular intervals and video.

As part of the assessment I would like to simulate different strip widths. 

The issue is then how the strip widths may affect the estimation for animals living in groups. Then, it may be the case when the strip of pictures or video captures part of a group. 

It can be assumed that the animals out of the strip  (and of sight)  may be balanced with animals from another group inside the band. But I wonder if something can be done for get a more precise sstimation.

I would like to make simulations with DSsim, but as far as I understand, DSsim simulates groups of individuals as "points" with a group size as an attribute , and not as individuals clustered in the space.

An option would be to build a population object out of DSsim and then bring it as the population object to be surveyed in DSSim, but I don´t know if this is possible.

Any ideas or workaround are welcome.

messages.author: ba2513683f4e548a
messages.subject: Re: Simulation of objects in groups for DSsim
parts:
Thinking further about this point, I wonder if this workaround may work for simulation purposes in DSsim:


Build a square region (for ease of work), then build a density object, adding many hotspots. Each hotspots should work as a "group" to be surveyed, when actually in terms of DSSim one surveys individuals. Then one can apply the surveys with different strip widths to the population object.

If that could work, the question is how many "hotspots" DSSsim would allow in a density region...
